name: What is the difference between a tenant improvement allowance and a landlord-provided build-out?
description: TI allowance gives funds and tenant control, while landlord-provided means the landlord manages and pays for the build-out, offering less tenant control.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a tenant improvement allowance and a landlord-provided build-out?

acceptedAnswer.text: A tenant improvement (TI) allowance is a fixed amount of money the landlord provides to the tenant to fund the build-out, giving the tenant more control over design and finishes, but the tenant typically manages the project and covers any overages. A landlord-provided build-out means the landlord undertakes and pays for the construction, often based on a pre-agreed scope, offering less control but potentially simpler execution for the tenant. The practical tradeoff is between control and financial responsibility; a TI allowance offers flexibility but requires careful budget management.
